subject: general
question: In which of the following states is the Gambhira - a popular dance, performed using various wooden masks?
solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gambhira**

 
 
• One of the famous devotional dances of **West Bengal **is Gambhira.
 
• It is the sacred devotional dance performed by worshippers of **Shakti**.
 
• The dance is named so because it is performed in the dance hall of the **Chandi Mandir.**
 
• In this dance, there are **two main dancers,** who are accompanied by a chorus.
 
• The two main dancers perform the role of** nana (maternal grandfather) **and **nati (grandson), **respectively. 
 
• This dance is performed along with musical instruments, like harmonium, flute, drum, and Judi.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Garba - Popular dance of Gujarat**

 
 
• **​**Garba is a form of dance that originates from the** state of Gujarat** in India.
 
• The name is derived from the **Sanskrit term** **Garbha.**
 
• It is performed during the nine-day Hindu festival **Navaratri.**
 
• Garba is performed in a **circle** as a symbol of the **Hindu view of time.**
 
 
 
• **Ghoomar - Popular dance of Rajasthan**
 
 
• **​**Ghoomar is a traditional folk dance of **Rajasthan.**
 
• It was the Bhil tribe who performed it to worship **Goddess Sarasvati.**
 
• The dance is chiefly performed by veiled women who wear flowing dresses called** Ghaghara.**
 
• The word ghoomna describes the twirling movement of the dancers and is the basis of the word ghoomar.
 
 
 
• **Perini Sivatandavam - Popular dance of Telangana**
 
 
• **​**Perini Sivathandavam is an ancient dance form of **Telangana.**
 
• It originated and prospered in Telangana, during the** Kakatiya dynasty.**
 
• Perini is performed in honour of **Lord Siva**, the Hindu god of destruction.
 
• **Padmasri Dr. Nataraja Ramakrishna** was the person who revived this art form recently.
